# s288 — affected.py finds a map for the same commit in another worktree

When the worktree's own map is missing, `tests/affected.py` looks for a map recorded for the same HEAD in the other worktrees of the repository and uses it, so a fresh slice worktree can select tests at once.

**Findings:** v1.11 relay 2026-10-15: every new slice worktree starts with no `.venv/affected-map.json`, so `affected.py --run` exits 2 until a six-minute full discover runs there, even when the main checkout already holds a map for the same HEAD; s276, s282, s286, s271, s283 and s284 implementers all hit it · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-15** — Verified: a worktree with no map of its own borrows a map for the same HEAD from another worktree only when that worktree's src/ and tests/ have no uncommitted changes. The check is git --no-optional-locks status scoped to src and tests; a probe that fails counts as dirty, and .slicer/ edits do not count. Candidates are tried in git worktree list order, so the main checkout comes first. An explicit --map never borrows. With no usable sibling, a missing map still asks for the full suite and says no other worktree has a readable, clean map. Dogfood: with this worktree's own map moved aside, affected.py --run refused for e0885fb; which candidate failed was not checked, since reading the main checkout was outside the allowed read. Backlog idea, not built: record the cleanliness of the tree in the map itself. Counts: test_affected 33 OK; full suite 2006 OK (skipped=1); slicer check passed; git diff --check clean. Mutation check: 14 mutants, all red, each for a stated reason.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** sharing a map across different commits, writing to another worktree's `.venv`, and changing how a map is recorded.

## Why

A slice worktree is cut from `main`, so its HEAD equals the commit the main checkout's last full discover mapped. The map is keyed by SHA (`load_map`), so a map from another checkout at the same HEAD is exactly as valid. Today each new worktree pays a full discover first, which AGENTS.md now says in its Commands section.

## Files

- `tests/affected.py`: in `select`, when `DEFAULT_MAP` is missing and no `--map` was given, list the other worktrees (`git worktree list --porcelain`, read-only) and use the first `<worktree>/.venv/affected-map.json` whose recorded SHA equals HEAD. Print one line on stderr naming the map it used. A map for another SHA is ignored as today. It never writes there.
- `tests/test_affected.py`, `AGENTS.md` (the fresh-worktree sentence), `CHANGELOG.md`.
